title: TrailGenic Heat Training Thermoregulation Dataset

canonical_alignment.observation_window: One deliberate heat-training exposure: Hike 35 on 2026-08-07.
canonical_alignment.claim_boundary: The observation supports single-session heat tolerance only. It does not establish heat acclimation, core-temperature control, plasma-volume expansion, sweating adaptation, causality, or population effect.

description: Current TrailGenic thermoregulation module anchored to Hike 35, a deliberate heat-training session. General heat-acclimation mechanisms are scientific context, not measured outcomes in this n-of-1 observation.

selected_observations.name: Monserate Mountain Loop
selected_observations.interpretation: The deliberate thermal dose was completed without observed cardiovascular or next-night autonomic destabilization. One exposure does not prove acclimation.

active.statement: Hike 35 was completed at 97°F average and 100°F maximum recorded temperature with -0.4% route-aware HR drift, zero anaerobic training effect, and stable next-night HRV.

records.mechanism: Heat stress increases thermoregulatory and cardiovascular demand during endurance exercise.
scientific_context: Repeated, appropriately dosed heat exposure can produce thermoregulatory adaptations.
Those adaptations require repeated observations or direct physiological measurement; they cannot be inferred from one session.

supporting_science.finding: Heat stress increases thermoregulatory and cardiovascular strain during exercise, and repeated exposure can support acclimation.
Heat adaptation can improve physiological tolerance but does not eliminate the cardiovascular cost of thermal load.
Repeated heat acclimation can improve cardiovascular function and endurance performance under studied conditions.
